title: Norman Rockwell: a picked set
videoFormat: None: a gallery carousel following the Freedom from Want reel
caption:
You know these paintings. Most people don't know his name: Norman Rockwell.

1. Kids at the Window (1951) on the cover. Everyone's waving. Dad just pulled up with a new car (it was painted as a Plymouth ad).
2. They Remembered Me (1917). A World War I soldier, grinning over his parcels from home.
3. Christmas Trio (1923). Carollers giving it everything on a December 1923 Post cover.
4. Parade (1924). Tiny lantern bearers, one very proud marcher.
5. Boy and Girl Gazing at the Moon (1926). Also known as Puppy Love. Watch the dog.
6. Pipe and Bowl Sign Painter (1926). An old-time painter touching up a tavern sign of a man who looks a lot like him.
7. Running with Pie (1928). A hobo, a stolen pie and a dog right behind him.
8. Kiss (1931). A stolen kiss on a footbridge, buckets and all.
9. Freedom from Want (1943). The Thanksgiving painting that wasn't about Thanksgiving. It was one of his Four Freedoms.
10. Christmas at Union Station, Chicago (1944). Hundreds of travellers rushing home for the holidays. Try to find Santa.
11. New Television Antenna (1949). A brand-new TV antenna on a very old house.
12. Fishing. Grandpa did the fishing. Guess who's holding the catch.

Which one is your favourite? Save this for later.

notes: User-picked set from WikiArt. Full-bleed paintings, no frame, no text; all information is in the caption. Running with Pie and Kiss are vignettes on cream, so the cream shows at the edges. Fishing only exists at 457×600 on WikiArt and is upscaled 2×, so it is a little soft.
